title: Dolly-zoom camera stretch
blurb: A dolly-zoom camera rig on one WebGL 2 canvas where the camera moves backward as optical focal length zooms from 18 mm to 135 mm, holding a live foreground HTML card at 1:1 width while a background HTML scene layer and 3D corridor telescope behind it.
question: Can one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas move a virtual camera backward as focal length zooms in (keeping field-of-view width times distance constant) so a foreground HTML card holds its exact apparent width and stays clickable while a background HTML layer and 3D corridor expand behind it?
result: Measured in HeadlessChrome/160.0.0.0 (2026-11-27): all five live checks pass with 0 console errors at 412 px (DPR 2.625, 1.096 MP canvas, 12.91 MB peak across checks). In Keep 1:1 width mode across 18 mm to 135 mm, the foreground card holds 252.00 px width (scaleDelta 0.00 px) while the background DOM layer expands from 278.07 px to 1099.64 px (3.95x), and real pointer clicks hit the card shot buttons, input and Cue take button.
